defects.defect: Ten phases with the lookup and Jordan's inbox both inside: I count about 50 steps and 23.5 hours in the simplified form (the proposal says 48 and 22), so there is no slack, and as the cards are written it is about 43 hours. One slow firewall install or a failed T4 takes it past one plan.

The lookup goes live in A, but the test its own card lists as a prerequisite (a seeded mail must cause no hand-off to the research helper) cannot be run until F019 exists in wave B, so it is run twice and the first pass proves less than the card asks. It also brings T4, a hand-off the roadmap lists as unconfirmed, into the fullest wave.

The scheduling-tool rule is designed and built in the first phase and T7 (can a reminder be created from an iMessage turn at all) runs in the second. T7 is meant to come before any check is designed; if it fails, about four hours of plugin work has no user.

The exit test covers a note, a reminder and two planted instructions only. Calendar questions, the evening text, typed facts and the handbook folder are in the wave's goal and are never exercised at the exit, and no fallback is stated for the case where Q6 is answered no.

Eight cards, three new kinds of risk and the house-rules plugin built from scratch: about 43 steps and 22 hours on my count with every answer yes, and only with S5, S8, S10 and S11 (plus the one-plugin shape of S1, which is not listed). Seven of the eight are conditional on Q6, Q4, Q2 or Q10, so the plan is anywhere from about 10 to 22 hours and cannot be written until those are answered.

G009 is counted as placed but ships only as a rule on the scheduling tool; what the card is for (a text to the other parent, ask-and-relay) is not built in any wave, so a card is ticked off with nothing the family would notice.

No Mac or phone is paired in A to C, so the deny list and its posture-check lines have nothing to be tested against; it adds about an hour to the gate phase, which I already count at about 7.5 hours against the proposal's 5.
The exit test needs a PDF sent from the phone, but F002 stays switched off if Q8 part 2 is answered 'wait', and the exit test does not say what it becomes in that case.
The exit test proves the 07:00 text, the token, the separation and the firewall, but not the lookup or Jordan's inbox, both of which are in the wave's goal.

Wave A carries both the in-house plugin with T5 (S1 not taken) and a firewall that blocks by default with a rule for every existing program. I count about 48 steps and 24 hours for Tony's inbox alone (the proposal says 43 and 21) and about 52 steps and 25.5 hours once Jordan's inbox is added, which is over one plan; with the envelope and T10 it is about 27 hours.

With every answer yes it is nine phases, about 46 steps and 23.5 hours on my count (the proposal says 44 and 22), the largest wave C of the three and at the ceiling. Six of the seven cards are conditional, and the exit test assumes reminders are built with no fallback if Q6 is answered no.

G015 is listed in A but its lookup half is built in wave B, so the card is not complete when wave A is signed off. The order is right for the lookup's own test; the split has to be stated on the card so nobody reads A as 'mail done'.
The day-8 half of T1 is checked only at the exit gate, after the 07:00 schedule is already on, so its stated fallback ('before anything else is built on it') cannot hold: everything is built by then.

T4 is first run in wave B, where both the web helper and the lookup rest on it. A failure needs a change to a signed-off setting and stops the wave's two main features, with no early warning before the wave B plan is written.

Six build phases, about 43 steps and 21.5 hours on my count, and the gate phase still holds an open design choice (page fetches direct or through the proxy, and how far to widen the rule wave A put on the gateway), which is a decision, not a runbook step.
The rule on where notes may be written is put in the second phase 'if T6 leaves a need for it', but T6 runs in the third phase. The notes rule belongs after T6.

Typed facts are rendered in the last build phase, after notes are live, so T6's check that the family facts still load after a save has nothing to load, and neither that check nor wave B's hand-off canary is run again once real facts exist.

Hours are understated. The first phase puts a deny-by-default firewall for the whole Mac, the Google project, gog and the sign-in into 3.5 hours, with no check that texts, weather, search and the alerts still work once everything is blocked by default. I count about 47 steps and 23 hours against the stated 39 and 19.5, and about 26 hours with the coded connector check that the proposal says still fits.

The roadmap's gate for mail is not all inside the wave: there is no 30-day retention on the mail reader's records and no eval-only copy with a test mailbox, and the proposal's own note says tracing and retention are not in its hours. Adding them is about 1.75 hours and three steps, which puts A at the ceiling.

As in the dependency proposal, the lookup goes live in A before the research helper exists, so the seeded-mail test its card requires is only half run and has to be repeated in B, and T4 is added to a wave that is already full.

The exit test never touches the calendar connection, the one new private-data source this wave puts on a parent's own agent, and has no stated form if photos are held back by Q8 part 2. The hidden-instruction PDF test is also not run again after the calendar tool lands on the same agent.

The gate phase leaves out the secret egress proxy and leaves the Prompt Guard tripwire as 'built or waived' with no size. I count about 42 steps and 22 hours against the stated 34 and 18, and with the privacy-gate plugin kept it is about 26 hours, so the wave relies on S7 as well as S13 although only S13 is listed.
T5 in the first phase is said to show what the check is given for the mail send tool, but that tool does not exist until the email phase. The send-tool part of T5 has to move there.

Three kinds of write or send in one plan, the first output outside iMessage among them; about 38 steps and 21 hours on my count against 36 and 19. The exit test checks email only by blocked attempts and never shows that one 'email me this' actually arrives.
The envelope is conditional on T10 passing, but T10 is in no phase's test list.
The day-8 half of T1 is checked only at the exit gate, after the schedule, the lookup and Jordan's inbox have all been built on the token.

graft.what: Wave A's firewall in its cheapest form (one rule set that lets the mail connector reach Google only), with deny-by-default for every program moved to wave B's gate phase beside the proxy; on my count this takes about 1.5 hours out of A, so Tony's and Jordan's inboxes fit together at about 24 hours and 50 steps, and B rises to about 23 hours.

The Google sign-in on day one of the plan and the day-8 half of T1 as a go-live condition of the morning-text phase, not only an exit-gate check, with the token-independent work (scheduler switches, firewall, T8 and the sheet) filling the wait.

T4 run once in wave A as a probe on the main-to-mail pair with nothing switched on, so wave B's plan is written knowing whether hand-offs return; the lookup itself still goes live in B after the helper, as the base has it.
A named overflow rule for wave A: Jordan's inbox is the phase that moves to the start of wave B if A runs long, because the exit test does not depend on it.

In wave C, typed facts (F042) built in the same phase as notes and before them, with 'the family facts still load after a save' in that phase's go-live check and wave B's hand-off canary run again once real facts are present.

'Email me this' (F049) kept as a worked, conditional phase for wave C, used only if Tony says yes under Q3 and only when the calendar phases or reminders drop out, so that C is still a full plan (it is about 10 to 16 hours otherwise); its send-tool part of T5 runs after the mail-out server exists.
Wave C's exit test recalls the saved note in a new chat the next day, which crosses the 04:00 session reset and so proves the note really persists.
The note on what can start while wave A waits on Q8 or on day 8: wave B's gate and web-helper phases need nothing from A, so the wait does not have to be idle time.
